decisions.what: The Playground smoke test runs in a CHILD node process (`.x-agent-build/smoke/smoke-runner.mjs`, generated at run time), configured through a JSON file and answering through a JSON file. Its stdout/stderr are piped into the build log and never touch the parent's.
decisions.why: This process's stdout is the MCP stdio transport. @wp-playground/cli boots worker threads and an Express server and is under no obligation to keep quiet on fd 1, and a PHP-wasm fatal is a real crash. A child process makes both harmless: nothing it prints can corrupt the MCP wire and nothing it crashes can take the server down. It also makes teardown unconditional.

decisions.what: The smoke runner contains no PHP and no regexes. factory.ts generates the two PHP probes (registrationProbePhp, renderProbePhp) and hands them over in the config; the runner boots, runs them, and returns raw text; the parent parses the tagged payload and extracts any PHP diagnostic (readTagged, extractPhpError, interpretSmoke — all unit-tested offline).
decisions.why: The first cut embedded PHP inside a JS template literal inside a TS template literal and needed three levels of escaping to survive. A runner that only forwards bytes cannot be wrong about a PHP fatal, and every parsing rule stays testable without booting WordPress.

decisions.what: The smoke test speaks no HTTP at all. Both `GET /wp/v2/block-types` and `POST /wp/v2/block-renderer/{name}` are dispatched INSIDE the sandbox with `rest_do_request()` after `wp_set_current_user(1)`, and `do_blocks()` is run as a cross-check. `rendered_html` prefers the REST block-renderer output and falls back to do_blocks.
decisions.why: Honours the seam contract's 'NEVER write fetch outside companion.ts' without needing an exception, and skips all Basic-auth plumbing against a throwaway instance. It is still genuinely the sandbox's REST layer — the same controller a real editor calls.

decisions.what: The bytes that get smoke-tested and the bytes that get zipped are the same bytes. stagePackage() copies block.json, the render file, every `file:` reference in block.json and the sibling `index.asset.php` into `<dir>/.x-agent-build/plugin/<slug>/`, writes the one-line loader plugin next to it, and the sandbox mounts that directory as a plugin. packageBlock() then zips that same `<slug>` directory.
decisions.why: A smoke test that runs the working tree proves nothing about the package. This way node_modules, src/ and package.json are provably not in the tested artefact, and 'it worked in the sandbox' means 'this zip worked'.

decisions.what: wp_block_build_test RETURNS its failures as {built, smoke:{registered, rendered_html, php_error?}, failure:{code:'build_failed'|'smoke_failed', message, hint}} instead of throwing an XError.
decisions.why: The spec output shape and the M5 acceptance both require reading `smoke.php_error` on the failure path, which an error envelope cannot carry. The CONTRACT.md §7 codes build_failed / smoke_failed are preserved verbatim in failure.code, so nothing is lost. Bad ARGUMENTS (missing dir, no block.json, static block.json) still throw invalid_input as usual.

decisions.what: Dependency cache: `<workspace>/.deps/<sha256(devDependencies)[0:16]>/node_modules` plus its package-lock.json. The first scaffold installs normally, then its node_modules is MOVED into the cache and symlinked back; later scaffolds with the same dependency set get the symlink and `npm ci` is used when the cached lockfile applies. `X_AGENT_BLOCK_CACHE=0` opts out; `force_install: true` forces a fresh install.
decisions.why: A cold `npm install` of @wordpress/scripts is ~1529 packages and 44 s. Keying by the devDependencies hash means a changed @wordpress/scripts range gets a fresh install rather than a stale tree. Measured: 56.5 s cold, 11.1 s warm.

decisions.what: wp_block_install re-reads the zip and checks it against the ENTIRE CONTRACT.md §5 install policy locally, before the posture probe and before any POST. A violation is {code:'invalid_input'} carrying `reasons: string[]`.
decisions.why: The companion answers 422 block_policy with the same reasons list. A round trip to a real instance should never be how the agent first learns that its own package is malformed, and the same inspector runs on our own output inside wp_block_build_test.

decisions.what: The posture gate reads `GET /fingerprint` (introspect tier, non-mutating) FIRST and throws errPostureForbidden('/blocks/install') before the multipart body is built. CompanionClient.installBlockBytes has its own assertToolchain guard; this one is in front of it.
decisions.why: The requirement is 'send NOTHING that would mutate', which is a stronger promise than 'the far end refuses it'. The client-side guard only fires once posture is already known, so something has to establish it, and /fingerprint is the cheap route the contract designates for exactly this.

decisions.what: The live sabotage test proves 'nothing was sent' two ways: (a) structurally — the Runtime it uses has no resolvable connection config at all, demonstrated in the same test by calling wp_manifest on it and asserting {code:'invalid_input', message:/Missing connection config/}; wp_block_build_test is `local: true`, so any attempt to reach an instance would have surfaced the same way. (b) observationally — broken-card never appears in GET /blocks/library and no pre-existing entry disappears.
decisions.why: (a) is race-free and is the real proof. The exact library-equality check that (b) started as was flaky: the toolchain instance is shared with other tracks' live suites in this repo and another suite legitimately installed `testimonial@1.0.0` mid-test. Asserting 'ours never appears, theirs never disappears' is the assertion that actually means something on a shared instance.

decisions.what: The live suite is gated on `X_AGENT_FACTORY_LIVE=1`, not the generic `X_AGENT_LIVE=1` the M3/M4 live suite uses.
decisions.why: Observed in practice: another track ran `X_AGENT_LIVE=1 npx vitest run ../tests/live` and picked up this file, which installs a block onto a real instance and moves its epoch underneath their tests. Vitest's root is x-agent/ and every track shares it, so a suite with side effects on a shared instance must have its own switch.

decisions.what: block.json lives at the SCAFFOLD ROOT (not src/), carries `editorScript: file:./build/index.js` and `render: file:./render.php`, and wp-scripts keeps its default `src/index.js` entry.
decisions.why: The install policy requires block.json at the block root of the zip. Keeping it out of src/ also stops wp-scripts' block.json auto-entry detection from firing, so the build stays the plain single-entry webpack build and its output shape is predictable.

decisions.what: adm-zip is bound through `createRequire(import.meta.url)` behind a hand-written minimal interface, exported as `loadAdmZip(): ZipCtor`. @wp-playground/cli is located by walking up from the module looking for `node_modules/@wp-playground/cli/index.js` or `tools/node_modules/@wp-playground/cli/index.js`, with an `X_AGENT_PLAYGROUND_CLI` override.
decisions.why: adm-zip ships no .d.ts and @types/adm-zip is not installed; @wp-playground/cli is installed under tools/node_modules, which Node resolution from x-agent/mcp/src cannot reach. mcp/package.json is not this track's file to edit, so both are resolved at runtime instead of by adding dependencies. `tsc --noEmit` stays clean and nothing is typed `any`.

decisions.what: The smoke sandbox binds the first free port in 9440-9449, overridable with X_AGENT_SMOKE_PORT_RANGE ("9460-9469") or pinned with X_AGENT_SMOKE_PORT / the tool's `port` argument. Timeouts: X_AGENT_BLOCK_BUILD_TIMEOUT_MS (default 15 min) and X_AGENT_BLOCK_SMOKE_TIMEOUT_MS (default 5 min), each overridable per call via timeout_ms / smoke_timeout_ms.
decisions.why: Several agents share this machine and tools/README.md splits the port space. The build timeout has to tolerate a cold ~1500-package npm install on a slow network, so it is generous by default and configurable, as required.

decisions.what: The factory is registered with `registerFactoryProvider({ create: (ctx) => new BlockFactory(ctx.logger) })` at the top of mcp/src/factory.ts, and the tool handlers reach it with `asFactory(await getFactory(ctx))`. No file owned by the core track was edited.
decisions.why: Seam contract note 2(b) in context.ts. Lazy construction, and wp_disconnect disposes it for free.

deviations.what: NONE on the build. The real `wp-scripts build` runs — `npm install` then `npm run build` -> `wp-scripts build` -> webpack 5.109.2, emitting build/index.js + build/index.asset.php. No fallback build path was written and none was needed.
deviations.detail: The spec allowed falling back to a hand-produced artefact of the same shape if a real wp-scripts build proved impractical here. It did not: @wordpress/scripts ^34.0.0 installs (1529 packages, 44 s cold) and builds in 1.2-2.7 s. Recorded explicitly so nobody has to wonder.

deviations.what: SUBSTITUTION for the final clause of M5 acceptance 1 ('wp_compile of a tree using agent/pricing-card is all_valid'). wp_compile exists (the session track landed it) but returns {code:'harness_gap'} for a freshly installed agent block. The equivalent was asserted instead, exactly as the fallback permits: POST /validate returns valid:true and epoch_ok:true at the NEW epoch, agent/pricing-card is present in GET /manifest at the new epoch, and POST /render of markup using the block returns the implemented HTML.
deviations.detail:
ROOT CAUSE, found and confirmed, and it is NOT in this track. An installed agent block lives in `wp_upload_dir()['basedir']/x-agent-blocks/{slug}/` per CONTRACT.md §5. WordPress's register_block_script_handle() builds a script's URL with plugins_url(), which only understands wp-content/plugins (and, since 6.4, theme dirs). For a block outside both it produces a mangled URL. Observed verbatim in the harness page served by the instance after a successful install:
  <script src="http://127.0.0.1:9400/wp-content/plugins/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/x-agent-blocks/pricing-card/build/index.js?ver=6a25dcff17fc32459dc7">
That 404s, so registerBlockType never runs client-side, __registry() lacks agent/pricing-card, and wp_compile correctly reports harness_gap rather than serialising something wrong. The block itself is fine: it IS in the harness's server-side bootstrap, it IS in /wp/v2/block-types, and POST /render produces the right HTML. The fix belongs in x-companion, where the block is registered — e.g. filter the metadata's script URL (block_type_metadata_settings / register_block_type_args) to point at wp_upload_dir()['baseurl'] for blocks it installed. Nothing in the agent-side factory can correct it.

deviations.what: RESOLVED, was a deviation earlier in this work: the live toolchain instance is now BOOTED by factory-setup.sh (core-only/toolchain on port 9440), not adopted. During the first pass both toolchain slots were held by other tracks and the suite ran against an adopted instance, restoring it afterwards by deleting the block and asserting the fingerprint returned to its exact pre-install value.
deviations.detail: factory-setup.sh keeps both behaviours: it boots when a (profile, posture) slot is free and adopts a live instance otherwise, recording `booted_by_us`. The afterAll cleanup only fires for an adopted instance, so a self-booted one is left with the block installed for inspection and is torn down with `--stop`. `stop.mjs --all` is never used; only instances this script booted are stopped, and only ports 9440-9449 are ever bound. NOTE for whoever runs this next: other tracks stop and re-boot instances in the shared tools/.runtime/ slots while you work — a runtime descriptor can vanish underneath a long-running probe. Boot your own and capture evidence in one process.

deviations.what: Both tools' output schemas are SUPERSETS of the shapes declared in registry.ts. wp_block_build_test adds `failure`, `package`, `timings_ms`, `deviations`; wp_block_install adds `previous_fingerprint`, `manifest_refreshed`, `session_reloaded`.
deviations.detail: The registry documents that a ToolDef whose name matches replaces the declared entry wholesale, schemas included, so this is a supported extension rather than a violation. Every field the registry declared is still present with the same type and meaning.

deviations.what: wp_block_install's session reload is best-effort and never creates a session.
deviations.detail: It calls getSession only when ctx.session already holds a warm instance, so the epoch reload (the provider's onEpochChange hook) fires for an existing harness page but installing a block never launches a browser as a side effect. A throw from the reload is logged and swallowed — the install already succeeded, and reporting it as a failure would be a lie. `session_reloaded` in the output says which happened.

deviations.what: KNOWN LIMITATION, environment-level, does not affect any M5 acceptance: on a single long-lived Playground instance, INSTALL AFTER DELETE fails with HTTP 500 install_failed 'Could not move the extracted block into the library.' First install and repeat install (the replace path) both work.
deviations.detail: Reproduced deterministically on a freshly booted core-only/toolchain instance with one script: install #1 -> 200 replaced_previous:false; install #2 -> 200 replaced_previous:true; DELETE -> 200 with the epoch restored exactly; install #3 (identical zip, seconds later) -> 500 install_failed. Afterwards the host filesystem shows uploads/x-agent-blocks/ EMPTY and the x_companion_block_library option is [], so nothing is stale on the host or in the database — the stale state is inside the sandbox. tools/playground/boot.mjs runs `wp-playground-cli server` with 6 worker threads, each with its own PHP-wasm NODEFS view of the mounted /wordpress directory; a directory rename performed by one worker is not reflected in another's cached nodes, and requests round-robin across workers, so the rename() inside WP_Filesystem_Direct::move() fails for the worker that handles the next install. Making it worse by hand confirms the direction: deleting uploads/x-agent-blocks/ on the HOST while the instance runs makes even wp_mkdir_p() fail ('Could not create /wordpress/wp-content/uploads/x-agent-blocks'), which is only possible if the worker is reading a cached node rather than the host. NOT an agent-side defect: the same zip installs fine before the delete, and wp_block_install surfaces the companion's WP_Error faithfully as {code:'companion_error', status:500, wp_code:'install_failed'} — which is the correct behaviour for a 500 from the far end. Candidate fixes, both outside this track: boot Playground with `workers: 1` for install-heavy scenarios (runCLI accepts it; boot.mjs does not currently expose it), or have x-companion fall back to a recursive copy+unlink when rename() fails.

notes_for_the_proof_suite_author: Run the live suite with: `cd x-agent && eval "$(./tests/live/factory-setup.sh --export)"` then `cd mcp && npx vitest run ../tests/live/factory.test.ts --no-file-parallelism`. The gate is X_AGENT_FACTORY_LIVE=1 (NOT X_AGENT_LIVE) plus tests/live/.factory-instances.json. `./tests/live/factory-setup.sh --stop` stops only what it booted.

factory-setup.sh needs BOTH postures: a toolchain instance for the install and a production instance for the posture_forbidden assertion. It uses ports 9440-9449 only, is idempotent (re-attaches rather than leaking a second instance), and adopts a running toolchain instance when both (profile, posture) slots are taken.

wp_block_scaffold and wp_block_build_test are `local: true` — they need NO connection config and touch no instance. Only wp_block_install talks to WordPress. That is the whole shape of the safety gate: the expensive verification is local, and the network step is a dumb upload of something already proven.
The block dependency cache lives at `${X_AGENT_BLOCK_WORKSPACE:-$TMPDIR/x-agent-blocks}/.deps/<hash>`. Delete it to force a cold-install timing measurement, or set X_AGENT_BLOCK_CACHE=0.

The smoke sandbox needs @wp-playground/cli. It is found at tools/node_modules/@wp-playground/cli by walking up; if the proof suite runs from somewhere that cannot see it, set X_AGENT_PLAYGROUND_CLI to its index.js. There is no degraded path — without a real Playground boot nothing gets packaged, by design.

KNOWN COMPANION BUG, blocking the harness half of M5 acceptance 1: installed agent blocks get a mangled editorScript URL (plugins_url() applied to a wp_upload_dir() path), so they never register client-side and wp_compile answers harness_gap. See deviations[1] for the observed URL and the suggested fix. Server-side rendering, /manifest, /validate and /wp/v2/block-types are all unaffected.

The toolchain instance is shared with the other tracks' live suites. Any assertion of the form 'the whole library / the whole fingerprint is unchanged' will flake; assert 'our thing never appeared' and 'their things never disappeared' instead.

DO NOT script install -> delete -> install against ONE long-lived Playground instance; the third step fails with 500 install_failed and it is a sandbox artifact, not a contract violation (see deviations[5] for the full reproduction and the two candidate fixes). First install and repeat/replace install both work reliably. Use a freshly booted instance per install scenario, or boot Playground single-worker.

The shared tools/.runtime/ slots are contended: another track stopped a core-only/toolchain instance and removed its runtime descriptor while a probe of mine was mid-flight, and factory-setup.sh once booted a second production instance because its state file had been deleted. Boot your own instance and capture everything you need inside one process rather than across several shell invocations.
